senses.gloss: m. (גטט, cmp. חטט) [engraving,] a legal document.—ג׳ אשה (often without אשה) letter of divorce. Pl. גִּיטֵּי נשים.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 1:5">Gitt. I, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 1:4">4</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ג׳ חוֹב</he> (usu. <he>שטר</he>) note of indebtedness.
B. Kam. 95ᵃ; Keth. 51ᵇ.—ג׳ חֲלִיצָה a certificate stating compliance with the law of ḥălitsah (Deut. XXV, 5—10).
Ib. 106ᵇ דמקרי גט חליצה who pronounces the words to be said at the act of ḥălitsah (Deut. XXV, 7 a.
<cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:8">8</cite>).—<he>ג׳ מִיאוּן</he> a certificate stating a woman’s protest against her marriage.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 11a:6">Snh. 11ᵃ</cite>.—<he>ג׳ מעושה</he> a document (of divorce) made out under compulsion.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 9:8">Gitt. IX, 8</cite>; a. fr.—[For other compounds see respective determinants].—
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 2:5">Ib. II, 5</cite> a woman may write <he>את גִּיטָּהּ</he> her own letter of divorce.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 2:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>להביא את גִּטָּהּ</he> to carry her letter of divorce.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 7:3">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>הרי זה ג׳</he> the letter of divorce is valid.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 7:3">Ib.</cite> <he>אינו ג׳</he> it is not valid.
Ib. ג׳ ואינו ג׳ it is of doubtful validity.—Pl. גִּטִּין, גִּיטִּין; constr. גִּטֵּי, גִּיטֵּי. Ib. III, 2; II, 2; a. fr.—Hence Gittin, name of a Talmudic treatise.
